claim: with no awarded rows the check concludes inconclusive BEFORE the currency half, which the docstring says needs no award to be judged and which is evaluated over all rows. So #68/#70 can never be verified fixed by the currency half alone, and rule 10 opens a repair_check obligation on a filed row.

the walk accepts a `simulation_mode` property anywhere in the spec, REQUEST bodies included, while the docstring's whole point is that every occurrence today is prose inside a request body and no RESPONSE publishes it. A new settings endpoint taking simulation_mode in its request would turn this green with the defect untouched. The comment asserts a distinction the code does not make.

probes the first 20 distinct card_ids and then prints the universal 'every card we hold a position in resolves'. Reachable today, not hypothetical: this account holds 39 event-card positions. population reports how many positions exist but never how many were probed, so the verdict cannot even be read as a sample.

docstring claims a change wakes EVERY open tab EXACTLY ONCE; the test subscribes one listener and reads one item. A notify() that delivers twice per listener passes (the queue is never checked for emptiness) and one that wakes only the first of several passes (only one exists). The sibling test already uses pytest.raises(queue.Empty) -- the pattern is in the file and unused here.

accepts any three of four scope fields, so a scope block with no `identity` passes -- and identity is exactly the field that answers the module docstring's open question, 'or it is scoped to an identity our API key is not'. The declared `right` lists three specific fields the assertion does not require any of. Secondary: with reported > 0 and no scope, the pass sentence ends in a colon and nothing.

asserts Write, Edit, MultiEdit and Bash are in the matcher, but protect_state.py handles six tool names -- NotebookEdit and PowerShell too. Delete |PowerShell from settings.json and this stays green, and so does the shell-write test, because decide() calls the guard directly and never consults the matcher. Net: Set-Content state\ledger.json reaches disk with no hook in front of it, on the machine where PowerShell is the primary shell. Rule 4 unenforced with every guard green.

asserts `kind` only on the automated message; the human message is checked for `auto` not being True and for reply_to, never for kind. Nest the kind-keeping line under the auto branch in fetch_inbox and this stays green -- while the module's own rule reads a missing kind as UNKNOWN, so every human reply would be announced forever as unclassifiable, which is the one distinction the check is named for.

`ignored` is built only from schemas that are PRESENT: a missing schema coalesces to {}, a missing paper property to '', and an empty description never matches NOT_HONOURED. Rename or move ShortRequest -- the keys are FastAPI path-mangled, so a module move renames them for free -- and the check passes saying 'a caller that asks for paper is given paper', while population still reports 6 surfaces checked. No unmeasurable count and no len(found) gate, which the sibling twenty lines above does have. This row is filed as #82, so a false pass sends a fix verification.

the second disjunct of the assertion is true of every page the renderer emits: 'stale' occurs 8 times and 'stale_from' 43 times in dashboard/index.html, from TEMPLATE itself. So `'unknown key' in served or 'stale' in served.lower()` cannot fail. serve_html could emit a band that no longer names the freeze -- a blank sticky div, a changed wording -- and all three assertions would still hold.

compare() counts a row whose answer arrived but could not be timed as 'unanswered', so the report says 2 still unanswered about two messages the vendor DID answer. This printed a false line to the operator today: 'TELEGRAM asked 2, no answered question yet, 2 still unanswered'.

`filters` is a COUNT comparison (0 < len(filtered) < len(rows)), not a period comparison. Passes on a violation: ?period=30d returning 8 of 16 rows with four different headline_period values shrinks the count and reads as comparable. Fails while the contract holds: a non-200 or a correctly-empty filter makes filters false and emits 'does not narrow them' about a request that errored -- rule 8, a failed read is not an empty read.

cmd_watch's priming new_lines() call sits OUTSIDE the try/except that protects the loop, so a journal caught mid-write at start-up kills the watcher immediately. The alert is then silently off for the rest of the session -- the one failure this component exists to prevent.

the retry notice prints to STDOUT, and every stdout line of this command becomes a chat notification. Its own comment calls a half-written journal line 'normal', and a normal event must not page the operator. Belongs on stderr.
pairs() scans every event to find the matching a2a_intent, for each a2a_outcome: O(n^2) over a journal already past 1300 lines and appended to every 15 minutes.

docstring's contract is that a closed report records the AWARD (reward_amount); the predicate demands a PAYMENT signal (paid_at, or reward_status in paid/award_recorded/rewarded) and never reads reward_amount after the schema guard. Every closed row today carries reward_amount 1000, reward_status 'awarded', paid_at null -- the docstring's contract holds exactly and the check fails. Secondary: the reason string has no verdict branch, so a PASS carries the defect sentence, and verify.py puts that in the body sent to the vendor.
compare() calls pairs(events) once per channel, doing the whole pairing twice.

count is compared against len(cards) with no notion of a page. A titled feed of 20 rows stating count 57 FAILS and tells the vendor 'an agent told to match a headline cannot' -- a headline defect that does not exist. qa/measure.py::collection_size exists in this repository for exactly this and names report #52, which went out because a check counted 200 rows against a stated 569. In the other direction, a feed that stops publishing count makes the reconciliation vacuous.

the AST scan globs [qs]*/**/*.py, so qa/ and scripts/ only, while the failure message states a universal. A writer under .claude/hooks/ -- which holds real Python that reads the journal today -- or under tests/ would never be looked at.

the docstring's headline is that a pass stopped in the middle leaves a RED test; the assertion only fails on verdict=='real' and not fixed, so every gap with verdict null passes. Reproducible on the committed file at this moment: 7 gaps, all verdict null, all fixed false -- a pass stopped between step 2 and step 4 -- and the check is green on it. Its pass sentence self-contradicts: 'settled all 7 gap(s) it claimed, 7 of them still awaiting a vote'.
_telegram and _a2a re-execute correspond.py and a2a.py from disk on every state() call, so the CLI pays two module executions per status.
_bug(events) takes an events argument it never reads; it works off the ledger.

the pass sentence claims both reconciliations held when either may have been skipped unmeasured: with total_earned_definition absent the per-hunter loop never runs yet the sentence says 'every hunter's total_earned matches the None it is defined as'; with active_hunters != len(entries) the valid-report comparison is skipped yet the sentence prints the leaderboard's own figure on both sides. Exactly the shape repaired as T01 and quoted in test_pipeline_verify.py. Pass reasons on this claim reach the vendor.

the reachability predicate accepts ANY status with a JSON content-type, so a recipe naming a path that does not exist passes: this platform 404s with application/json, proven by our own evidence store (evidence/sha256/00/004111a9... is GET /api/v1/cloned-bot/create -> 404 application/json). The widening comment justified dropping the 200 with the 401 case and wrote a predicate covering every status. The one defect report #76 exists to catch, in its commonest form -- a stale or misspelled path -- now passes, under the sentence 'every path a /build recipe sends an agent to is callable'.

'awarded' is defined as reward_status != 'pending_award' -- a whitelist of one exact string, where the comment says 'a row is awarded when the tracker does not call it pending'. Rename their status to 'pending' or 'awaiting_award' and every zeroed row becomes an award of 0 outside its published band; the check then fails and sends a FAIL verification against #68/#70 for a state their own answer created.

verdict FAILED on any non-200, with a sentence saying the recipe's first step fails. A 429 from their rate limiter or a 503 mints a defect about a step nothing was established for. The sibling check in the same file concludes inconclusive on non-200, and test_attribution_to_a_wallet_is_provable was repaired for exactly this on 2026-09-07. volatile=True does not save it: the marker is recorded but read by neither findings.py nor fold.py, so the failure opens a finding like any other.

failure requires the counter to parse to 0; an ABSENT field gives None, and None == 0 is False, so a summary that stops publishing total_predictions/total_volume passes while stating 'the summary's counters are non-zero beside 38 position(s)' about two values it never read. qa/measure.py::required exists for exactly this and is not used. Filed as #83, so a false pass leaves as a fix verification.

the docstring claims TWO properties -- one control name everywhere, AND omission never spending real money -- and the verdict reads only the first. `found[label]['not_honoured']` is computed and never referenced again in the function. The violating state is named in the module docstring itself: the exchange endpoint defaults to live on omission. Once it gained a `paper` property this check went green regardless.

the docstring's contract is that the text is on the journal BEFORE the request leaves; the assertions run after main() returns and observe nothing while the POST is in flight. Move the a2a_intent append down into the timeout handler after client.post and the check stays green -- while a process killed mid-POST loses the text, the only failure the two-event record exists for. The mock's request handler is the place that could read the journal and does not.

docstring says there is no value enumeration ANYWHERE; the assertion allows up to three alternatives (arg.count('|') < 3). regex_set:(DELTA|STAT|CORR) passes while being exactly the extractor shape the phantom-injection test in the same file exists to condemn. Nothing justifies the threshold and every other clause in the file is absolute.
